facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man presented with a painful nodule on the lower part of his right leg
the lesion had been stable in size and painless for 4 years but had enlarged and become tender over the past 6 months
an irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm was noted just above the lateral malleolus of the right leg
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy was present
there were no other suspicious cutaneous lesions
Routine blood tests, including complete blood count, fasting blood sugar, liver and renal function tests, were within normal limits
Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV were negative
a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass partly covered by skin, measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields
Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45
The tumor cells were negative for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31

concepts.why: The presence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma, along with strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45, is consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei, along with mitotic figures, is consistent with leiomyosarcoma.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei, along with mitotic figures, is consistent with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
The focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45 is consistent with melanoma, although the lack of other characteristic features makes this diagnosis less likely.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei, along with mitotic figures, is consistent with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei is consistent with solitary fibrous tumor.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei is consistent with liposarcoma.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei is consistent with myxofibrosarcoma.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei is consistent with pleomorphic lipoma.

rationales.F02: The lesion's recent growth and tenderness suggest a possible malignant process, which is more consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans than with other listed concepts.
rationales.F03: The mass's size, shape, and location are non-specific and do not rule in or out any of the listed concepts.
rationales.F09: The presence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma is highly suggestive of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
rationales.F10: The high mitotic rate and presence of atypical mitotic figures suggest a malignant process, which is more consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans than with other listed concepts.
rationales.F11: The strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45 are consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, but the absence of S-100 protein staining rules out melanoma.
rationales.F12: The absence of staining for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31 helps to rule out other listed concepts, such as melanoma, leiomyosarcoma, and solitary fibrous tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The lesion's history of being stable for 4 years before enlarging, its firm and mobile nature, and the histological findings of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells support Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, with Leiomyosarcoma as a close runner-up due to similar histological features but less matching clinical presentation.
